title: AES-GCM in EnvelopedData is explicitly rejected with a descriptive error, not silently mishandled
description: decrypt.rs detects ID_AES_128_GCM and ID_AES_256_GCM OIDs in the content encryption algorithm position of an EnvelopedData and returns SmimeError::UnsupportedAlgorithm with the message 'AES-GCM in EnvelopedData is not supported; use AuthEnvelopedData'. A future contributor might remove this branch or collapse it into the generic 'unknown OID' fallback. That would be wrong: AES-GCM legitimately appears as an OID in the RFC's OID registry, so falling through to the generic error would produce a confusing message. The explicit rejection with an explanation is a usability and correctness guard — it tells the caller exactly why decryption failed and what the correct structure is (RFC 5083 AuthEnvelopedData), which is non-obvious.
